name: Memoir
hint: A chapter of a life around one question: the then-self lives through it, the now-self understands what it meant.

parts.title: Before
chapters: The moment
Open with a scene from the book's most charged moment, unexplained, so the reader feels the question the book carries.
The question
Let the now-self step forward briefly: what you are trying to understand, and why you are writing it now.
Life before
The place, the people and what the then-self believed and wanted, in concrete scenes rather than background.
The first sign
A small event that pointed ahead in hindsight, written as the then-self lived it.

parts.title: What happened
chapters: The turning point
The event that splits life into before and after, as a full scene with senses and dialogue.
New rules
How everyday life changed: summarise the weeks, but stay in scene wherever something is at stake.
The people around you
Those who helped, betrayed or simply stayed, each shown through something they did.
What you didn't say
What you hid from others or from yourself, and what it began to cost.

parts.title: The reckoning
chapters: The hardest part
The lowest point, written without sparing yourself and without the now-self offering comfort.
The truth
A conversation, a letter or a discovery that makes it impossible to go on as before.
The choice
What you did, and how the then-self understood it in the moment, before hindsight.

parts.title: What it meant
chapters: Afterwards
The consequences, as honest about what went wrong as about what went right.
Understanding
The now-self looks back: what you see today that you couldn't see then, and what is still unresolved.
Back to the moment
Return to the opening scene or place and show what has changed in you.

name: Non-fiction
hint: The reader's problem, a clear promise and one idea per chapter, with evidence and examples, until the reader can use it.

parts.title: The promise
chapters: The reader's problem
Open with a concrete situation in which the reader recognises their own problem.
The promise
Say what the reader will be able to do, know or understand after the book, and how the book will get them there.
Why it's hard
Show why the usual answers fall short. This is where you earn the reader's trust.

parts.title: The foundation
chapters: What you need to know first
The concepts and facts the rest of the book rests on, and nothing more.
The first idea
One claim stated plainly, with evidence, an example and what it means for the reader.
The second idea
The next claim, built on the first. Show the link in the very first paragraph.
A case in depth
A case, a person or an experiment that shows the ideas at work in real life, from start to finish.

parts.title: Going deeper
chapters: The third idea
The most surprising or difficult idea, now that the reader has the footing to take it in.
The case against
The counterarguments and where knowledge runs out. Honesty here makes the rest of the book stronger.
Common mistakes
How it usually goes wrong, and how readers can spot the signs in themselves.

parts.title: Putting it to use
chapters: How to do it
Concrete steps in order that the reader can take as soon as tomorrow.
When it doesn't go to plan
The most common obstacles along the way, and what the reader does then.
Conclusion
Tie back to the promise from the start: the essentials in brief, and the way forward.
